steps.body: $|W|=|X\times Y|=xy$, so $|E|=|\mathcal P(W)|=2^{xy}$.

Each of the $z$ elements of $Z$ independently picks one of $2^{xy}$ images:
$$|E|^{|Z|}=\left(2^{xy}\right)^{z}=2^{xyz}.$$

steps.title: Purpose

cse-2006-cs-8.approach: Assume positive-edge D flip-flops. Since $f$ changes only at negative edges, the fastest $f$ toggles once per clock period, i.e. $f$'s period is at least $2T$; a delay of exactly one clock period $T$ is therefore a $180^\circ$ phase shift of $f$. Find the circuit that delays $f$ by exactly $T$ without inversion and without race.

steps.title: What 180° means here
steps.body: $f$ changes only at negative edges, spaced $T$ apart, so $f$ toggles at most once per $T$ and its period is $2T$ (fastest case). Delaying $f$ by $T$ = half of $f$'s period = $180^\circ$.

steps.title: Circuit C
steps.body: FF1 (clk) samples $f$ at the positive edge, half a period after $f$ changed — data is stable, so $Q_1=f$ delayed by $T/2$. FF2 (inverted clk) samples $Q_1$ at the next negative edge, another $T/2$ later. Output $=f(t-T)$: a clean $T$ delay, i.e. $180^\circ$.

steps.title: Why the others fail
steps.body:
**A** and **D**: FF1 is clocked by $\overline{clk}$, i.e. at the negative edge — exactly when $f$ changes, a setup/hold race, so the output is unreliable; they also pass the data through $\overline Q$.

**B**: same timing as C but with $\bar f$ fed in, giving $\overline{f(t-T)}$. For the fastest $f$, $\overline{f(t-T)}=f(t-2T)=f(t)$, i.e. $0^\circ/360^\circ$, and in general it is an inversion, not a delay.

optionAnalysis.reason: FF1 samples on the negative edge when $f$ itself changes (race) and the result is inverted twice in an unreliable way.
Delays by $T$ but outputs $\bar f$; that is an inversion, not a $180^\circ$ delay of $f$.
Correct: posedge then negedge sampling gives a clean delay of one clock period = $180^\circ$ of $f$.
FF1 clocked on the negative edge with $f$ changing at that same edge — race; output also inverted via $\overline Q$.

pitfalls: Reading 180° as half a clock period — the phase refers to $f$, whose period is at least two clock periods.
Ignoring the race when a flip-flop samples on the same edge at which its input changes.
cse-2006-cs-8.verification: Timing diagram for $f$ toggling each negative edge: C's output is $f$ shifted by one clock period, which is the complement of $f$, i.e. $180^\circ$ out of phase.

cse-2006-cs-15.approach: Trace the loop: the update `i /= 2, j += i` adds the already-halved $i$ to $j$, so $j=\lfloor n/2\rfloor+\lfloor n/4\rfloor+\dots$, a geometric series bounded by $n$.

steps.title: Trace

Start $i=n,\ j=0$. Each iteration (body empty) runs the update: $i\leftarrow\lfloor i/2\rfloor$, then $j\leftarrow j+i$. Loop stops when $i=0$.

Example $n=16$: $i=8,j=8$; $i=4,j=12$; $i=2,j=14$; $i=1,j=15$; $i=0,j=15$.

cse-2006-cs-19.approach: Rewrite each language by its block structure and see how many independent counts must be matched: one nested pair is CF, two simultaneous cross-constraints are not.

steps.title: L1 is CF
steps.body: $0^{n+m}1^n0^m=0^m\,0^n1^n\,0^m$: nested matching (outer $0^m\dots0^m$, inner $0^n1^n$). Grammar: $S\to0S0\mid A,\ A\to0A1\mid\epsilon$.

$L_2=\{0^a1^a0^m: 0\le m\le a\}$. Take $w=0^p1^p0^p\in L_2$ and $w=uvxyz$, $|vxy|\le p$, $|vy|\ge1$; $vxy$ touches at most two adjacent blocks.
- $vy$ within blocks 1–2: pump down ($i=0$) — either blocks 1 and 2 become unequal, or both shrink equally to $a<p=m$, violating $m\le a$.
- $vy$ touches block 3 (blocks 2–3 or only 3): pump up ($i=2$) — block 3 exceeds $p$ while block 1 stays $p$, so $m>a$ or $\#1\ne\#0_1$.

Every case leaves $L_2$, so $L_2$ is not CF.
